claims.statement: The reviewer is registered in langgraph.json as `reviewer` (openswe.graphs.reviewer:traced_reviewer_agent), which serves read-only access to threads created before Managed Deep Agents. New runs use ReviewerKind through the Managed Deep Agents framework.
The reviewer agent is strictly read-only on the repository: its prompt forbids commits, pushes, and gh pr review / gh api reviews, and its toolset omits every commit/push/PR-opening tool.

ReviewerKind in the MDA framework constructs the reviewer per run with a reviewer-only toolset (fetch_review_diff, add_finding, update_finding, list_findings, publish_review, resolve_finding_thread, reply_to_finding_thread plus read helpers), via PrepareReviewerRunMiddleware for sandbox/checkout/diff prep.

The reviewer configures a single reviewer subagent with REVIEWER_SUBAGENT_SYSTEM_PROMPT that works with a partition and returns candidate defects only; the subagent cannot call finding or publication tools and the parent validates, records, and publishes.

PrepareReviewerRunMiddleware performs deterministic non-LLM setup before the first model call: it ensures the sandbox with abandon_unreachable=True, mints and caches a repo-scoped GitHub App installation token as a bot token, and clones-or-fetches plus force-checks-out the PR head via prepare_review_repo.

The reviewer computes a unified diff and the set of in-diff (file, line, side) tuples during run prep and passes both as diff_text and diff_line_set in run state so add_finding can validate at creation time rather than at GitHub-publish time.

The reviewer run prep gathers context concurrently including PR title/body, existing PR review threads, the saved repository custom style prompt, org guidelines, root and scoped AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md from the base ref, an API-standards skill, and an optional review scout walkthrough.

Author-controlled inputs (PR title/body, existing review-thread comments, finding replies) are wrapped in XML data blocks whose closing tags are neutralized by _escape_for_data_block and whose logins are validated against the GitHub username grammar, so a PR body cannot break out of its wrapper or inject instructions.
Finding surface states only ever move forward, so normalization of a legacy record reconciles contradictions by taking the furthest-along state.

add_finding rejects any finding whose start_line..end_line range is not part of the PR diff, returning success:false with in_diff:false so the model does not re-anchor or retry; out-of-diff findings are disabled.
add_finding resolves diff context from run state first, then configurable, then a fresh fetch_pr_diff, and stores an extracted diff_hunk on the finding when diff text is available.

publish_review batches findings above the severity threshold (default medium, status open, capped at REVIEW_FINDING_CAP) into one GitHub PR Review with a fixed host-formatted summary line and one inline comment per surfaced finding, appending a fenced suggestion block when present.
Each published inline comment embeds an open-swe-review-comment JSON marker so later runs can re-locate the finding's GitHub thread by finding id.

After posting, publish_review stores GitHub comment/thread ids back on each finding, resolves GitHub threads for findings moved to resolved via the GraphQL resolveReviewThread mutation, and advances the reviewer thread's last_reviewed_sha to the reviewed head.

publish_review returns a structured result the model must inspect because success:true alone does not confirm a posted review: skipped_empty_re_review with review_id null means a skipped empty re-review, dry_run:true means eval-mode simulation, and unresolvable_findings lists findings that could not be posted.

reconcile_findings_with_review_threads syncs tracked findings against current GitHub review-thread state before each run: it records new comment/thread ids and marks findings surfaced, folds a finding to resolved when all its threads are resolved or outdated, and captures the latest human reply as a needs_reassessment interaction with a reconciliation note.

Reviewer threads are tagged with REVIEWER_THREAD_KIND = reviewer in their metadata (always written by set_reviewer_thread_metadata), which is how findings storage, usage rollups, and the review UI locate reviewer threads.

The reviewer opts into abandon_unreachable=True for its sandbox because the sandbox holds only a checkout re-derived each run and the durable findings live on the thread, so an unreachable sandbox is abandoned rather than bricking reviews on that PR; only when sandbox creation itself fails does the run die with a typed on-PR notification.
A missing reviewer thread is converted to a structured do-not-retry tool result because retry cannot restore evicted, evaluation-mode, or never-created durable finding state.
The repository custom-style prompt is injected into the reviewer prompt when available, retrieved fail-soft from the REVIEW_STYLES store.
